title: Work done in a worktree session reaches backlog.py cost as work rows
goal: A session that claims, lands or works an item from a git worktree outside the clone's checkout (../it-ops-kb-worker2) leaves work rows that distill delivers and backlog.py cost --rework reads, so an item's cost is not zero: the capture of a worktree session spools where the clone's readers look (ql_base.places sets the spool under the checkout the running _tools sits in, and bl_cost.open_lines and distill read only the clone's own spool and the main worktree's). Answers the SP-tpulmoxh retrospective: every item read 0 runs and 0 prompts, and land warned 'landed with no work rows' on each worker2 item.

run:
import json,os,shutil,subprocess as sp,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
S=Path.cwd();t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());c=1
try:
    g=lambda *a,cwd:sp.run(['git','-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@t',*a],cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,check=True)
    m,w=t/'it-ops-kb',t/'it-ops-kb-worker2';m.mkdir();g('init','-q',cwd=m)
    shutil.copytree(S/'_tools',m/'_tools',ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__','fixtures'));g('add','-A',cwd=m);g('commit','-qm','i',cwd=m)
    g('worktree','add','-q','-b','work/ST-abcdefgh',str(w),cwd=m)
    i='ST-abcdefgh';u=dict(input_tokens=1,cache_creation_input_tokens=2,cache_read_input_tokens=3,output_tokens=4)
    (t/'tr').write_text(chr(10).join(json.dumps(r) for r in [dict(type='user',promptId='p1',message=dict(role='user',content='x')),dict(type='assistant',requestId='r1',message=dict(model='claude-sonnet-5-5',usage=u,content=[])),dict(type='user',promptId='p2',message=dict(role='user',content='y'))])+chr(10))
    e=dict(os.environ,CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=str(w));e.pop('CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA',None);e.pop('CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT',None)
    def h(**k):sp.run([sys.executable,str(w/'_tools'/'querylog.py'),'capture'],input=json.dumps(dict(dict(session_id='s1',cwd=str(w),transcript_path=str(t/'tr')),**k)),text=True,cwd=w,env=e,capture_output=True)
    h(hook_event_name='UserPromptSubmit',prompt_id='p1',prompt='x')
    for v in ('claim','done'):h(hook_event_name='PostToolUse',prompt_id='p1',tool_name='Bash',tool_response=dict(stdout='ok'),tool_input=dict(command='python3 _tools/backlog.py %s %s'%(v,i)))
    h(hook_event_name='UserPromptSubmit',prompt_id='p2',prompt='y')
    sys.path.insert(0,str(m/'_tools'));import bl_cost
    L=bl_cost.open_lines(str(m))[0];print('work lines for',i,':',[l for l in L if l.get('item')==i]);c=0 if any(l.get('item')==i for l in L) else 1
except Exception as x:print('check error',type(x).__name__,str(x)[:150])
finally:shutil.rmtree(t,ignore_errors=True)
sys.exit(c)

notes: Housekeeping 2026-10-06: the -k worktree_session_work_rows selector named a test the suite rules no longer allow; the check builds a temporary clone with a linked worktree, replays a worktree session's hook events (claim, done, two prompts) through querylog.py capture and asks bl_cost.open_lines of the clone for the item's work line; it exits 1 today. Root cause found by the housekeeping: _tools/ql_base.py places() keys the spool on the checkout the running _tools sits in, so a worktree session spools beside its own worktree; the reader side (bl_cost.open_lines, bl_base.main_worktree_spool, ql_distill) reads only the clone's and the main worktree's spool. _tools/ql_base.py joins the touches for that; if the fix lands on the reader side instead, _tools/bl_cost.py, _tools/bl_base.py and _tools/ql_distill.py need adding first.
